title: Shortest Unique Prefix for Each Word
statement: You are given a list of distinct lowercase words in which no word is a prefix of another word. For each word, its shortest unique prefix is the shortest leading substring that no other word in the list begins with. Return a list of these shortest unique prefixes, one per input word, in the same order as the input. Because the words are distinct and none is a prefix of another, every word always has such a prefix (in the worst case the whole word itself). If the input list is empty, return an empty list.
hints: You repeatedly ask 'how many words share this leading substring?' — which structure lets shared prefixes share storage so you can answer that in one pass down the characters?

Insert every word into a trie, and at each node keep a counter of how many words pass through it; a node with count 1 is reached by exactly one word, so the path to it is a prefix unique to that word.

After building the trie, walk each word character by character: descend into the child, append the character, and the moment the node you just entered has count 1, stop and emit the accumulated prefix. Append the character BEFORE testing the count so the deciding character is included.
